note: Two adjudicated variants: one of the orthography class and one capital accent. Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero divergence beyond them, and there is no accidental comparison against tpl, whose profile is substantive-only.

adjudicated.ruling: Prǽlio, with do. Prælium and proelium are the same noun: proelium is the older spelling and prælium the one the liturgical books print, and the dictionaries head both. Both analyzers link the corpus's lemma, so nothing is lost by printing what the 1962 witness prints.

House rule (ORTHOGRAPHY.md): accents ARE printed on capitals. Ím-pe-ret has three syllables and the stress falls on the first; do omits accents on capitals throughout, as at ordinarium.confiteor-sacerdotis w038.
